subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in session PIN gate that blocks tools until a trusted TypeScript verifier marks the current SessionEntry authenticated, or should this remain plugin-owned?
rationale: The code seam is clear, but this changes core auth/config/secret/session-state semantics and cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Sponsor core PIN gate
options.body: Define the secret source, verifier path, persisted session bit, reset semantics, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep plugin-owned
options.body: Rely on before_tool_call or trusted tool policy plugins unless a missing plugin API is proven.

options.title: Defer to broader auth design
options.body: Leave the issue open but block implementation until session auth is designed with gateway/device auth boundaries.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core PIN gate
recommendation.body: Define the secret source, verifier path, persisted session bit, reset semantics, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available routing signal from current blame across the inspected surfaces plus adjacent auth-profile session-state work.
